instruction.text: Select where all the bees are gathered.

end.text: This is a beehive. Beehives can be home to up to 60,000 honey bees. They are often built into trees, rocks or other small places that offer natural protection. Bees produce honey inside their hives.

instruction.text: Select the hole behind the meerkat.

feedback.end: A meerkat’s home is called a burrow. Burrows are made up of underground tunnels that lead to larger rooms, where meerkats can sleep and cuddle. There are many entrances and exits in case of danger.

instruction.text: Select the shell on top of the hermit crab.

feedback.end: Hermit crabs sleep and live in their shells. They can be very picky when it comes to deciding which shell they want, trying on many different ones before finding their new home.

instruction.text: Select the pile of sticks and logs.

feedback.end: This is a beaver dam. Beavers chew and shape trees and branches to make their homes. Their dams create still water that helps warn them if any predators are coming.
You might have seen a hole like this in the forest before. This is a badger sett. Larger setts can have up to 100 metres of tunnels and as many as 40 different entrances and exits!
